topic: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth
hook: This machine is almost a light-day away.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, cold starlight, deep blacks and warm gold foil
world: Space-age realism: deep interstellar space in cold starlight, Jupiter up close, and on Earth a desert radio dish and a mission control room at night
through_line: the Voyager probe's white dish antenna, farther from home in every block

cast.Engineer: a woman in her 40s, short black hair, rectangular glasses, navy polo shirt, plain blue lanyard

props.Voyager: the Voyager space probe: a white 3.7-metre dish antenna, a ten-sided body wrapped in gold foil, a long thin boom and a short boom ending in a dark cylindrical power generator

places.Deep space: deep black interstellar space, a dense field of faint stars, the Sun a tiny bright star far behind
places.Dish: a giant white radio dish antenna on a desert plateau at night, low hills, a few small service lights
places.Control room: a dim mission control room, rows of desks with blank glowing monitors, a large dark wall screen

blocks.narration: This machine is almost a light-day away. Next month, it crosses that line, the first thing we ever built to do it.

shots.visual: The Voyager probe's white dish antenna sliding past the camera in Deep space, a glint of sunlight flaring on its rim
beats: the dish slides past, close enough to touch
a glint of light flares on its rim

shots.visual: The tiny Voyager probe alone in Deep space, the Sun a small bright star far behind it
The Voyager probe turning slowly in Deep space, its long boom and gold-foil body catching faint starlight
beats: its dish swings toward a tiny blue dot

blocks.narration: Voyager one launched in nineteen seventy-seven, swung past Jupiter and Saturn, then crossed into interstellar space in twenty twelve.

shots.visual: A tiny bright point of rocket fire climbing into a pale dawn sky far above a calm seaside horizon, trailing a long thin curving column of white smoke, the rocket itself too distant to see
beats: the point of fire climbs higher
the smoke trail curves and spreads

shots.visual: The Voyager probe gliding past the giant striped cloud bands of Jupiter, a great red storm swirling below
The Voyager probe crossing a faint rippling veil of glowing blue gas into Deep space
beats: the probe passes through into darkness

blocks.narration: Its radio runs on about twenty watts, a fridge light bulb. Giant dishes on Earth strain to hear it.
blocks.visual: A faint signal and a giant dish

shots.visual: The Voyager probe's dish antenna in Deep space sending a faint thin pulse of light toward a tiny blue dot
beats: a faint pulse of light leaves the dish

shots.visual: The giant Dish on its desert plateau at night, slowly turning to point at the stars
beats: it tilts up and locks on

blocks.narration: Its plutonium power fades every year. So engineers keep switching parts off, one by one, just to keep it talking.
blocks.visual: Power fades; engineers switch systems off

shots.visual: The Voyager probe's dark cylindrical power generator at the end of its boom in Deep space, a faint orange glow fading
The Engineer at her desk in the Control room at night, pressing a key on her keyboard
beats: a green light on her console blinks off

shots.visual: The Engineer leaning back in her chair in the Control room, watching her monitor

blocks.narration: A radio hello takes nearly a day to reach it. Say hi this morning, and it hears you tomorrow.

shots.visual: A thin pulse of light rising from the giant Dish on its desert plateau into the night sky
beats: a pulse of light leaves the dish
it races up into the stars

shots.visual: The Voyager probe's dish antenna in Deep space as a faint pulse of light arrives and its rim glints
beats: the pulse of light reaches the dish

captions.hook_line: Next month Voyager 1 becomes the first thing we ever built to sit one light-day from Earth 🛰️
captions.body: Voyager 1 launched in 1977, flew past Jupiter and Saturn and crossed into interstellar space in 2012. On November 18, 2026 it reaches one light-day from Earth, about 16.1 billion miles, so a radio signal takes a full day each way. Its transmitter runs on about 23 watts, and as its plutonium power fades, engineers keep switching systems off to keep it talking.
